subject: Region binding handover and data provenance Q&A
messages:

Cc: Security Team <security@finserve.com>; Legal Ops <legal.ops@finserve.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T08:14:00Z
Subject: Dedicated deployment — region binding & handover process

Alex — thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production pilot and have a couple of tight asks from our security and legal teams before we proceed. High-level: we need a documented handover process for region pinning (formal steps when we request a region bind), proof that data storage and backups remain within the pinned geography, and an operational playbook for tenant-level permanent deletion.

Two quick questions to start:
- When we request a region pin for a tenant, what exactly changes at the infra level and how long does ORP (operational region pin) take to complete?
- Can you provide an end-to-end diagram (storage, snapshots, backups, monitoring, logs) annotated with where data can cross boundaries, if at all?

If you can send a short write-up and any artifacts (diag/CSV) we can share with our SecOps and Legal, that will speed approval.

Thanks —
Mike
Director, Cloud & Security
FinServe Corp

From: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finserve.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T12:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment — region binding & handover process

Mike — great questions. I’m attaching a concise set of artifacts that map to each ask and a one-page operational summary. See attachments: region_binding_matrix.csv (states, AZs, snapshot policy), data_flow_diagram_v2.png (end-to-end), and redwood-dedicated-erase-playbook.pdf (tenant deletion steps).

Short answers up front:
1) Region pin changes: tenant routing and storage affinity are updated in our control plane. Specifically, we update routing policies so new writes are anchored to the selected region, and we adjust snapshot/replication targets to prevent cross-region replication for that tenant. No immediate live data migration is triggered unless requested — we can do an optional migration job if you need historical objects moved. Typical operational window for a non-migration pin is ~30 minutes (propagation, control-plane locks, and verification).
2) Data crossing: By default, system-level telemetry and aggregated metrics are processed in our control plane (hosted) but payloads, model I/O, and tenant customer data remain in the pinned region for Dedicated deployments. The diagram annotates the minimal telemetry flows and where we redact payloads.

I’ll loop in Kimberly for the finer security details around backups and wipe proofs; Rishi will outline the snapshot/replication constraints for model KV caches. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if your team prefers.

—Alex
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finserve.com>
Cc: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment — region binding & handover process

Mike — following Alex’s summary, a few clarifications from Security:

- Backups/snapshots: For a region-pinned tenant we disable cross-region snapshot replication at the tenant level and mark existing replicated snapshots for scheduled deletion per your retention window. Our standard behavior is to keep a tenant-scoped snapshot retention policy separate from cluster-level DR snapshots; the matrix shows which snapshot sets are tenant-scoped vs cluster-scoped.

- Physical locality & encryption: All persistent disks and object storage containing tenant payloads are provisioned in the pinned cloud region. Data at rest is encrypted with customer-specific keys (if configured) or per-tenant keys stored in our KMS. We can add HSM-backed keys via your KMS provider as part of the Private deployment addendum.

- Wipe and attestation: The redwood-dedicated-erase-playbook.pdf describes the three-step deletion workflow: (1) mark and quarantine tenant data; (2) run controlled purge (object-level delete + overwrite windows for ephemeral caches); (3) verify via hash-based proof and update audit log. We provide a signed attestation that includes purge timestamps, operator IDs, and snapshot UUIDs. Proof delivery SLA is configurable in Dedicated contracts (standard: 7 days; expedited: 48 hours).

- Telemetry & control plane: The only metadata that may leave the pinned region is aggregated scheduling telemetry (non-PII). We maintain session-level keys in-region and scrub payloads before any hosted analytics.

I included an excerpt from the erase playbook as inline bullets below your diagram for quick review. If FinServe requires custom retention/erase timelines, we can add contract addenda for compliance.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finserve.com>
Cc: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-01T14:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment — region binding & handover process

Mike — adding a commercial note to align expectations:

- Region pinning without data migration: no additional infra charge beyond a small one-time orchestration fee (covering verification & manual checks).
- Optional migration (historical data move) is scoped and quoted based on dataset size and encryption needs.
- Attestation SLA upgrade (48h) is available as a Dedicated add-on; I’ll include the pricing sheet if you want it.

If this matches your expectations, we can prepare a short SOW that adds the region-binding acceptance criteria and attestation SLA to your order form.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@finserve.com>
To: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, legal.ops@finserve.com
Date: 2028-07-02T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated deployment — region binding & handover process

Alex / Kimberly / Neha — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple follow-ups from Legal/SecOps after reviewing the artifacts:

1) Legal wants the attestation to include the exact list of snapshot UUIDs removed or marked for deletion when migration is requested. Is that feasible?
2) SecOps asked whether we can get an automated daily export (S3) of the audit log for tenant deletion events (to a FinServe-controlled bucket) for the pilot period.

If both are doable we’ll onboard for the pilot and sign the SOW addendum. Could you confirm feasibility and the expected delivery timelines?

Thanks —
Mike
Director, Cloud & Security, FinServe Corp
